title: Farm to Table — School Health & Wellness Kiosk
subject: Skill Education

blocks.text: ACTIVITY 1 • SET UP A SAFE KIOSK
Build and test a safe counter for your future kiosk. Use empty clean utensils and teacher-approved practice water. Do not prepare or serve food in this activity.
Show clean handling • Arrange three zones • Practise passing and pouring • Improve your plan after a teammate checks it.
WONDER BEFORE YOU WORK A counter looks tidy. Does that prove it is safe? Name one thing you would check that a photograph cannot show.
Watch the demonstration. Ask before you act.
Build, test, swap roles and improve.
Explain one change. Get teacher feedback.
Evidence to keep: a counter map, a tool-practice record and one improvement.
My role first: ______________  One skill I want to practise: ______________
Five practical steps • Work with your teammate • Record real results
Follow the teacher’s handwashing demonstration. Cover hair, secure aprons and check the work route. Identify when hands must be washed again.
One moment when I must wash again: ______________________________
Check each actual item for cracks, sharp damage, dirt and stability. Report problems; set rejected items aside for the teacher. Keep chemicals away.
Label RECEIVE & WASH, PREPARE and SERVE. Place tools for each task. Mark separate places for used tools, waste and records/payment. Draw your map on page 50.
Pass a spoon handle-first. Hold a cup away from its rim. Use a jug to pour 100 mL of practice water into a cup over a tray. Swap roles. Do not drink the practice water.
Ask a teammate to follow the route without crossing clean and dirty tasks. Change one position if needed, repeat the trial, then clean and reset as instructed.
STOP • CHECK • ASK THE TEACHER If a tool breaks, water spills or the layout feels unsafe, pause the task. Keep others clear and tell the teacher. Restart only after the issue is resolved.
I COULD DO THIS ANOTHER WAY…
Suggest a different safe arrangement. What would you keep the same to compare both plans fairly?
Human Services • Draw what your team actually sets up
Label the three zones. Add arrows for work flow. Show the handwashing point, visitor route, waste, used utensils and a separate records/payment place.
DRAW AND LABEL YOUR COUNTER HERE
TEST YOUR DESIGN WITH A TEAMMATE
Can everyone reach the tools safely?
Do clean and dirty tasks stay separate?
Can a visitor move through without crowding?
MY FIRST PLAN → MY BETTER PLAN Choose one change from your trial. Explain how it made the counter safer or easier to use.
Human Services • Real observations are more useful than perfect answers
Wash and dry hands as demonstrated
Check tools and report a problem
Pass a spoon safely; avoid cup rims
Keep clean and dirty tasks separate
Target: 100 mL. Use the jug markings with teacher guidance; practise over a tray.
During service practice, your spoon falls onto the floor. What will you do before using a spoon again?
One change I made after feedback, and why it helped:
Counter map reviewed • Hygiene demonstrated • Tool practice observed Ready for the next activity / Revisit a skill  (Circle and discuss.)
Ask fairly • Count carefully • Choose thoughtfully

Work in a team of three. Invite up to six classmates to share their preferences, record anonymous tallies and design a menu with one snack and one drink. Your teacher checks the options before the survey and the final plan before food preparation.
WONDER BEFORE YOU WORK If your favourite snack gets the fewest votes, how could you make a fair menu decision? Give one reason beyond “I like it”.
Ask without influencing • Record one response per person per question • Compare totals • Explain a safe, practical menu choice.
Check choices and practise the invitation.
Explain your decision and get feedback.
MY KIT: picture cards, pencil, tally sheet, blank menu card and colour pencils.
READINESS: Activity 1 checked • Teacher approves survey location and options.
ACTIVITY 2 • FIVE STEPS TO A MENU
Most of the session is for doing: 42 of 60 minutes
With the teacher, choose two possible snacks and two drinks. Use pictures or short descriptions. Consider available ingredients, suitable preparation and cost. Write options A and B on page 54.
Say: “Would you like to help us plan our kiosk? You may skip any question.” Ask: “Which of these two options would you prefer, or neither?” Use the same wording and choices each time.
One phrase we must avoid because it pushes a choice: __________

Invite up to six classmates once each in the teacher-approved area. Record only tally marks: A, B, neither or skipped. Do not record names or reasons for personal food restrictions. Swap team roles after two invitations.
Add each question’s tallies. Check its total matches the number taking part. Compare A and B, noting ties, neither and skipped. Discuss safety and practicality with the teacher.
Draft your menu on page 55. Show dish names and ingredients clearly. Ask a teammate to read it and suggest one change. Teacher approval is needed before any preparation.

RESPECT & PRIVACY Participation is optional. Accept “no” politely. Do not collect names, phone numbers, medical details or photographs. Direct private allergy or dietary concerns to the teacher. No tasting in this activity.
DID YOU KNOW? • ONE GROUP IS NOT EVERYONE
Six classmates give you a small snapshot of preferences. Another group might choose differently. Why should we avoid saying “the whole school prefers this”?
What will you do if many classmates choose neither?
Human Services • Record real responses, including skipped questions
Invited: ______   Took part: ______   Declined: ______ Check: Took part + Declined = Invited. Target: up to six classmates.
QUESTION 1 • WHICH SNACK WOULD YOU PREFER?
Question 1 total: ______  Does it match “Took part”?  Yes / Recheck
QUESTION 2 • WHICH DRINK WOULD YOU PREFER?
Question 2 total: ______  Does it match “Took part”?  Yes / Recheck

KEEP THE COUNT FAIR Add one tally in one row for each participant per question. “Neither” is a choice; “skipped” means no answer. A person who declined the whole survey is not counted in these tables.
Among A and B, our snack result was: A more / B more / Tie / No A or B votes.
The difference between snack A and B totals is ______ votes.
Human Services • Use evidence, explain a choice and improve your design
A tie or few responses? Explain your next step; do not invent votes.
Add dish names and ingredient lists. Use a clear picture and readable lettering. Keep prices as “to be calculated”. Avoid claims such as “chemical-free” or “cures illness”.
Maths helped us __________________. Language / art helped us ______________.
Garden connection: a possible crop is __________. The teacher must check its suitability and preparation before use.
The most popular option needs equipment your school does not have. How could your team respond?
TEACHER CHECK • Options suitable • Tallies checked • Ingredients reviewed Menu plan: Approved for next activity / Revise first  (Circle and discuss.)
Before preparation, the teacher confirms allergy arrangements, ingredient safety, quantities, storage and equipment. A vote does not establish food safety.
No-fire preparation • Measured ingredients • Thoughtful portions

Use your teacher-approved menu to prepare a small trial batch of one snack and one drink. Measure ingredients, assemble safely and compare portions. This is a supervised classroom trial before the kiosk opens.
WONDER BEFORE YOU WORK Three bowls look equally full. Does that mean they contain equal amounts? How could you check without guessing?
Read a recipe • Measure mass and volume • Mix and portion safely • Record actual amounts • Explain one improvement.
Compare results and get teacher feedback.
READY? Activity 2 menu approved • Three zones ready • Ingredients checked Teacher confirms allergies, storage and permission before any tasting.
Worked example for three small trial portions • Teacher approval required
Use these examples only if approved for your group. If your menu differs, the teacher supplies an adapted recipe and quantities before you start. These are tasting portions, not a complete meal.
Teacher cooked, cooled and stored safely

Gently combine with a clean spoon. Divide into three bowls using serving utensils. Teacher may approve a little washed, prepared dhania; record any addition. No raw sprouts or raw palak/methi in this example.
Measure, combine and stir in a clean jug. Divide the finished drink into three small portions. Do not assume each is exactly 100 mL: lemon juice adds to the batch. Record what you actually serve.
MEASURE WITH THE RIGHT TOOL Use a scale for grams (g) and a graduated jug or measuring spoon for millilitres (mL). An ordinary spoon is not a reliable measuring spoon.
TRY THE MATHS • PLAN FOR SIX
To make six equal trial portions, multiply each recipe amount by ______.
Chickpeas: ______ g   Cucumber: ______ g Water: ______ mL   Lemon juice: ______ mL
Same recipe / Adapted recipe  (Circle.)  What changed, and why?
Keep your record nearby, away from the food counter
Wash and dry hands, secure hair and apron, and check the three zones. Teacher clears the ingredients and tools. Set aside anything damaged, unapproved or uncertain.
Teacher ingredient clearance received: ______  Start time: ______
Place an empty bowl on the scale and press Tare / Zero before weighing. Read liquid markings at eye level with the jug on a level surface. Record planned and actual amounts on page 59.
Follow the approved recipe in order. Mix the snack gently with a clean spoon. Stir the drink separately. Keep utensils in their own zones. Swap roles with clean hands.
One step where our teamwork helped: _______________________
Use clean serving utensils. Weigh each snack portion in a tared bowl. Use a clean measuring jug to measure drink portions before serving. Record and compare the amounts.
Our agreed portion target: Snack ______ g  Drink ______ mL
Ask the teacher to approve the trial before any tasting. Label ingredients and cover the food. Teacher decides safe serving/storage and leftovers. Sort approved scraps, clean up and wash hands.
Finish time: ______  One reset task completed: _______________

SAFETY FIRST • NO GUESSING No heat or sharp-tool use by students in this activity. Never taste to test whether food is safe. Use a fresh tasting utensil for each taste, only with teacher permission; never return it to the shared food.
DID YOU KNOW? • WHAT TARE DOES
Tare removes the empty container’s displayed mass, so the scale shows the food added. What mistake would happen if you forgot to tare?
What could explain a difference between the recipe amount and what we served?
Human Services • Measure carefully and record honestly
Scale tared? Yes / Recheck   Liquid reading checked at eye level? Yes / Recheck
Use the same measuring method for each portion. Teacher agrees the target first.
Food / drink left in the mixing containers: _______________________________
COMPARE • EXPLAIN • IMPROVE Largest snack portion: ______ g. Smallest: ______ g. Difference: ______ g. A smaller difference can show more even portions; it does not prove food safety.
Human Services • Safe preparation, evidence and improvement
Hands, tools and work zones kept clean
Your teammate wants to add an unlisted ingredient to improve the taste. What must happen before it goes into the shared batch?
One change to make our next portions more even, and how I would check it:
Garden crop / none: ______________  Teacher crop clearance: __________
Teacher-approved next step for the prepared food: _________________________
Recipe followed • Measuring observed • Portion record checked • Reset completed Ready for service practice / Practise again  (Circle and discuss.)
Teacher background: FSSAI Food Safety at Home — fssai.gov.in/flipbook.php?bookid=31. Follow the school’s food-safety arrangements for ingredients, cooling, storage and service.
Welcome thoughtfully • Serve safely • Keep resources in use

Rehearse a friendly kiosk visit, serve a teacher-approved portion and guide returns to the right place. Record what happens, then improve your service. Use empty bowls or picture cards if food service is not approved.
WONDER BEFORE YOU WORK Look at the picture. Why are used cups returned away from the serving counter? What else would make this kiosk welcoming?
Explain ingredients clearly • Respect a visitor’s choice • Use serving utensils • Separate returns and waste • Use evidence to improve.
Confirm readiness and practise one service exchange.
Set up, role-play, sort, record and reset.
Compare results and get teacher feedback.
MY KIT: approved menu and ingredient card, clean serving utensils, bowls/cups, return tray, labelled sorting containers, pencil and record sheets.
READY? Activity 3 checked • Teacher approves food, service time and waste routes.
Team: __________  Mode: Food trial / Empty-container rehearsal
Complete one round, reflect and practise again
1 • SET UP TWO SEPARATE AREAS | 8 MIN
Keep the clean serving counter apart from used utensils and waste. Display the approved ingredients. Teacher checks the serving period, handwashing access and a clear visitor route.
Invite a visitor politely. Explain the snack or drink using the ingredient card. Ask whether they would like the approved portion. Accept “no”. Refer allergy questions to the teacher; never guess.
A welcoming sentence I will use: __________________________
Use a separate clean serving utensil for each food. Hold bowls on the outside and cups below the rim. Do not touch ready-to-eat food. With empty containers, rehearse the same actions.
One action that protected the food: ________________________
Thank the visitor and point to the return station. Use labels agreed with the teacher. Sort clean sample items or picture cards first. Do not reach into mixed waste; report sharp or unknown items.
One item whose destination I checked: ______________________
Record the round on page 63. Clean and reset as directed. Wash hands after handling returns or waste and before serving. Change any used gloves; gloves do not replace handwashing.
One improvement for the next round: _______________________

STOP • CHECK • CALL THE TEACHER Stop service if a utensil falls, food is touched or an ingredient is uncertain. The teacher decides the safe next step. Never return a visitor’s leftovers to the shared batch.
DID YOU KNOW? • CLEAN ROUTES MATTER
Hands and utensils can carry microbes from used items to ready-to-eat food. Why might a tidy-looking counter still need a better return route?
In round ____ I noticed __________________. Next time I will…
Mode: Food trial / Empty-container rehearsal   Teacher go-ahead: __________
Practise with one invited classmate, or let the teacher play the visitor. Change roles only after the counter is safely reset.
Write Yes, Not yet or N/A. Explain one observation below. A rehearsal checks our actions; it does not certify food safety.
Reset and washed hands before role change
A visitor asks, “Is this safe for my allergy?” You are not sure. Write what you would say and do.

Teacher references: FSSAI Safe food handling & Hygiene Booklet (fssai.gov.in/flipbook.php?bookid=151); EPA Composting at Home (epa.gov/recycle/composting-home). Apply the school’s food-safety and waste arrangements.
Prevent waste first • Reuse safely • Sort by local instructions
MATCH EACH ITEM TO ITS NEXT STOP
Use clean samples or picture cards. Discuss each route with the teacher. A material’s name or colour alone does not tell you where it belongs.

OUR SORTING KEY RETURN: reusable utensils for proper washing. COMPOST: only scraps accepted by our system. RECYCLE: only materials accepted by our collector. OTHER / UNSURE: ask the teacher. Do not assume every paper cup is recyclable or compostable.
Reusable cups issued: ____   Returned: ____   Still to locate: ____
Check: issued = returned + still to locate. If not, recount together.
One item we avoided using: __________  How we avoided it: ______________
How could offering a smaller first portion help? __________________________
If none was accepted, explain the route used instead: _____________________

DID YOU KNOW? • A LIVING RECYCLING TEAM Decomposers break down suitable organic scraps. Compost needs managed conditions; a bucket of fresh scraps is not ready plant food. Follow the teacher’s compost plan, including any limits for citrus and cooked food.
Maths helped us count __________. Science helped us explain __________.
TEACHER CHECK • Service observed • Routes checked • Records reviewed
Count honestly • Explain your choices • Celebrate learning
Work out the cost of one kiosk item, suggest a teacher-approved price and share your team’s learning at a classroom mini-mela or school Kaushal Mela. Use your records from Activities 1–4 as evidence.
WONDER BEFORE YOU WORK Two teams collect the same amount of money. Does that mean both made the same surplus? What other information would you need?
Separate cost from receipts • Calculate a cost per portion • Compare a plan with results • Explain a decision • Recognise value beyond money.
Check records and try the worked example.
Cost, price, design, rehearse and organise evidence.
Review feedback and complete teacher checks.
MY KIT: cost notes or teacher-supplied prices, recipe and portion records, calculator, paper, pencils and your project portfolio.
READY? Activities 1–4 reviewed • Teacher confirms presentation mode.
Our mode: Classroom simulation / Approved school event   Team: __________
Use one clearly defined batch of one item for your calculations
Choose one snack or drink. Record the cost of ingredients actually used, serving supplies and other agreed batch costs. Keep reusable equipment purchases separate. Teacher supplies missing prices.
Divide batch cost by the number of usable portions made. Discuss affordability and covering costs. Record a price only after teacher approval. Mark estimates clearly.
One reason for our proposed price: __________________________
Choose one record each for preparation, service and waste. Add your cost sheet. Label a garden-to-kiosk-to-compost connection using only crops and scraps actually approved.
Give a one-minute explanation: our need, our action, our evidence and our next improvement. Each teammate speaks. Ask one visitor or another team for specific feedback.
Label the evidence pages, tidy the display and return resources. Submit the completed portfolio. Teacher supervises any money handling and all actual food service.

SAFETY & HONESTY AT THE MELA A display does not require food tasting or sales. Use picture cards if food service is not approved. Never claim that a recipe cures illness, guarantees health or is safe for every allergy. Ask before photographing anyone.
DID YOU KNOW? • A PRICE IS NOT A PROFIT

Money collected is called receipts. The amount left after the costs counted in your sheet is the surplus. If costs are higher, there is a shortfall. What could cause a shortfall even when visitors like your item?
I CAN TRY IT ANOTHER WAY
If I repeated this project, I would change __________ because…
Mathematics in action • Keep planned and actual figures separate

TRY THE MATHS • A POSITIVE EXAMPLE Suppose a batch costs ₹120 and makes 12 usable portions. Cost per portion = ₹120 ÷ 12 = ₹10. At ₹15 each, selling all 12 gives receipts of ₹180. Surplus = ₹180 − ₹120 = ₹60. If only 6 sell, receipts are ₹90 and the shortfall is ₹30. These are practice figures.
Our item: __________________   Record type: Planned / Actual (circle)
Donated / garden ingredients and how we valued them: __________________
Do not call a donation “free to produce”. State if its value is excluded. Teacher checks our costing choices.
Usable portions made (N): ____   Cost per portion = A ÷ N = ₹________
Approved price (P): ₹____   Portions sold / planned to sell (S): ____
Receipts (B) = P × S = ₹________   Surplus / shortfall = B − A = ₹________
Free sample portions: ____   Unsold portions: ____   Recount: N = S + samples + unsold.
If no portions were made, do not divide by zero. For a free demonstration, receipts are ₹0; learning can still be valuable.
One reason our result differs from the example:
Our sheet excludes these costs, if any: __________________________________
Show what we did • Explain what we learned
Sketch a readable display. Include our item name, ingredients, four evidence labels and one improvement. Show sample prices only if approved. Use icons and short captions.
Visitor or teammate suggestion (no name needed):
We will use / adapt / not use this suggestion because…
Teacher check: evidence clear / revise first   Date: __________  Team: __________
Choose two gains: careful hygiene, confidence, teamwork, listening, measuring or less waste. Describe something you observed; do not claim a health improvement you did not measure.
CONNECT THE TWO FORMS OF WORK
Life Forms helped us __________________. Human Services helped us __________.
One subject I used: __________  The real task it helped me solve:
FINAL TEACHER REVIEW • Evidence reviewed • Practical skills observed
My next practice goal, agreed with the teacher: ______________________________
Recorded learning time: ____ hours   Presentation: Completed / To complete
COMPOSITE SKILL LAB • CONNECTING BOTH PROJECTS
From caring for plants to serving people
WONDER BEFORE YOU WORK A healthy-looking plant and an attractive food stall both need careful work behind the scenes. Which records would help you explain that work?
Choose records you made. Add page numbers and explain what each proves. An honest record of a problem and your improvement is useful evidence too.
A garden decision I changed after checking
A kiosk preparation or service record
A kiosk decision I improved after feedback
Complete the journey using what really happened. If a crop was not used or a scrap was not accepted, explain the alternative.
One teacher check that protected this journey: __________________________
COMPOSITE SKILL LAB • CONNECTING BOTH PROJECTS
Apply your learning when the plan changes

THE CHALLENGE Your team expected 12 visitors, but 18 arrive. Your garden harvest is smaller than planned. You have ingredients for only 12 agreed portions. Teacher approval covers those ingredients and portions. What could your team do fairly and safely?
Expected visitors: ____   Actual visitors: ____   Extra visitors: ____
One thing we must check before changing the plan:
You may suggest a non-food demonstration, later service or a teacher-approved change. Do not dilute a drink or reduce portions without checking with the teacher.
What we would say to a visitor who must wait or cannot be served:
Maths helps us __________________. Language helps us __________________.
Role-play test: one thing we will observe is ______________________________
TEACHER GO-AHEAD • Check any change before serving. Use a non-food role-play if food service is not approved.
COMPOSITE SKILL LAB • CONNECTING BOTH PROJECTS
Look at evidence • Discuss progress • Choose a next step
Together with the teacher, use: I = independently; P = with a prompt; N = needs more practice. These are learning notes, not an official CBSE grade scale.
Follow safety checks and ask when unsure
Select and use suitable tools carefully
Measure, record and check a result
Listen, share roles and respect others
Care for resources and improve my work
One practical skill demonstrated to my teacher: __________________________
Keep this workbook as a record of what you tried, checked and improved.
Apron and hair cover — Keep clothing and hair controlled — Ready / Recheck
Soap, safe water, clean drying provision — Wash and dry hands properly — Ready / Recheck
Three trays and labels — Separate receive, prepare and serve zones — Ready / Recheck
Bowl, spoon and covered container — Mix, portion and protect approved food — Ready / Recheck
Measuring jug, spoons and cups — Measure and practise controlled pouring — Ready / Recheck
Clipboard, pencil and tally sheet — Record observations away from food — Ready / Recheck
